function: Uplink channel estimation in near-field holographic MIMO with an unsupervised score-based MMSE estimator, plus PCA noise-level estimation (fully digital and hybrid) (pp. 2, 6-9).
system: Uplink: BS with 1024-antenna ULA (spacing lambda/6), single-antenna users, fully digital or hybrid analog-digital with random 1-bit combiners; fc = 16 GHz; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 10).
method: UNet denoising autoencoder (residual score form), unsupervised denoising score matching on received pilots only; closed-form MMSE estimator, and OAMP for hybrid systems (pp. 6-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: correlated Rayleigh fading with near-field one-ring spatial correlation (Eqs. 1-5), von-Mises scatterers; 50,000 training and 10,000 test samples; no standard or measured channel (pp. 3, 10).
test_conditions: Trained at ring position 1 (Table I); tested over SNR, then at unseen positions 2 and 3 with online adaptation over 2,000 pilot slots each (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, oracle MMSE (known covariance and noise), sample MMSE, sparsity-based noise estimator; no earlier learned estimator compared (pp. 10-11).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR, number of training samples, iterations and under-sampling ratio; noise-level bias, std, RMSE and percent error; runtime (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Big-O orders for fully digital and hybrid estimators (p. 9); runtime 2.5 ms vs 290 ms for oracle and sample MMSE, fully digital (Table III, p. 10).
q1_support: p. 3: "we have also adopted the correlated Rayleigh fading model"; custom near-field one-ring spatial-correlation simulator (Eqs. 1-5), with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "well trained offline for position 1 as described in Section V-A"; p. 12: "the online adaptation algorithm quickly recovers the performance to a remarkable level that is close to the oracle MMSE bound", for ring positions 2 and 3 never seen offline.
q3_support: p. 10: "The following baselines are compared in the simulations"; LS, oracle MMSE and sample MMSE are all non-learned, and no earlier learned estimator (supervised, SURE-based or generative) is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "the per-iteration complexity of the score-based estimator in hybrid analog-digital systems is"; Table III (p. 10) also gives runtimes of 2.5 ms and 17.2 ms.
q5_support: p. 10: "We consider uplink channel estimation in a typical HMIMO system whose general parameters are listed in Table I"; the data are generated by the authors' simulator, and no code or data link, DOI or public dataset is given.
notes: Area 2 (channel estimation). ris=0: holographic MIMO is a dense BS array (Fig. 1, p. 3); metasurface combiners appear only in footnote 3 (p. 4), and no RIS lies between BS and users. q2 rests on the online adaptation of Fig. 5 (p. 12); the noise-level error sweep and the training-set-size sweep (p. 11) do not count, and Fig. 6(c) (p. 12) varies the pilot ratio without saying whether the model is retrained.
